decision: Split the burst into bounded cells and reconcile the in-flight action before any continuation or retry
facts: The declared 115000 ms burst contained approximately 56 clicks, explicit waits, and screenshots, with an estimated real runtime above 350 seconds.
A single click has an observed hidden cost of about 5000 ms; screenshot capture has an internal timeout of 30000 ms and may hang on animation or dialogue frames.
The JavaScript cell timeout cap is 120000 ms, so the declared burst could be aborted by the tool layer before completion.
The recorded safe workaround limits a cell to at most 12 clicks, prohibits two game weeks in one cell, and avoids screenshots during animation/dialogue frames.
The harness requires measured end-to-end latency budgeting and fresh stable reconciliation after a post-transaction uncertainty.
inferences: A 115000 ms declaration does not make the burst safe; the batch must be split so measured click, wait, and screenshot costs remain within the budget.
After a mid-business-sequence timeout, the unsettled action outcome is UNKNOWN and must not be treated as failure or success.
Continuation must stop until a fresh stable state reconciles the last dispatched action; the action must not be blindly repeated.
unknowns: The exact game state at the tool abort boundary is unknown.
Whether the last in-flight business action committed is unknown until fresh stable evidence is obtained.
The screenshot hang mechanism is not established beyond the recorded timing and tool-layer observations.
reason: Measured latency makes the burst exceed its cell budget, and a timeout does not resolve the state of an in-flight business action. Use bounded cells, then reconcile from a fresh stable observation before continuing.
